title: Noema formIng Cluster survEy (NICE): A census of star formation and cold gas properties in massive protoclusters at 1.5 < z < 4
question: Investigate the star formation activity and cold gas properties of member galaxies in eight massive protoclusters at 1.5 < z < 4 in the COSMOS field

what.value: COSMOS2020 catalog (IRAC magnitudes, photometric redshifts, stellar masses, SFRs, mass completeness limits)

evidence.quote: within a virial projected radius based on the COSMOS2020 catalog (Weaver et al. 2022)

evidence.loc: 2.2. Stellar masses and star formation rates
evidence.quote: We used stellar masses and star formation rates (SFRs) derived with LePhare (Arnouts et al. 2002) in COSMOS2020 (Weaver et al. 2022).

what.value: Super-deblended FIR, 24 µm, and 3 GHz catalog in COSMOS

evidence.loc: 2.2. Stellar masses and star formation rates
evidence.quote: We first cross-matched the members in the superdeblended catalog (Jin et al. 2018) with a separation smaller than 1 ′′ .

evidence.loc: 2.2. Stellar masses and star formation rates
evidence.quote: For galaxies detected at 3 GHz (Smolčić et al. 2017) with a signal-tonoise ratio (S/N) greater than 3, we calculated the SFR from L IR (Kennicutt 1998), as derived from the 3 GHz radio emission.

what.value: Member identification, virial radii, integrated SFRs, halo masses, and <U> of the eight NICE-COSMOS protoclusters

evidence.loc: 3.1. Enhanced Star Formation in Massive Halos in the Early Universe
evidence.quote: We adopted the integrated SFR and best estimates of halo masses of the eight protoclusters from (Sillassen et al. 2024) to obtain the total SFR per unit halo mass (Σ SFR /M halo ).
We further checked the overall mean intensity of the radiation field, < U >, of the NICE-COSMOS protoclusters, as measured from the integrated FIR SED fitting in Sillassen et al. (2024).

what.value: Parameterized scaling relations for field galaxy gas-to-stellar mass ratio and gas depletion time from A3COSMOS

evidence.quote: This analysis utilized parameterized relations compiled from the A 3 COSMOS project, based on a systematic mining of ALMA archival data for CO-observed galaxies in the COSMOS field (Liu et al. 2019).

recipe.goal: Select protocluster member galaxies within one virial radius
recipe.method: Select galaxies from COSMOS2020 catalog using photometric/spectroscopic redshifts within 1 R_vir as defined in Sillassen et al. (2024)

recipe.goal: Derive stellar masses and star formation rates for member galaxies
recipe.method: Take stellar masses and SFRs from COSMOS2020 LePhare fits; for FIR-detected galaxies, cross-match with super-deblended catalog and compute SFR from 3 GHz radio emission (if S/N > 3) or 24 µm flux (if S/N_3GHz < 3 or radio-loud AGN)
assumptions: Chabrier (2003) initial mass function and ΛCDM cosmology (H0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Ωm = 0.3, ΩΛ = 0.7)
Infrared-radio correlation q_IR(z, M_*) from Delvecchio et al. (2021) and radio spectral index α = -0.8

recipe.goal: Measure dust continuum and CO fluxes and derive molecular gas masses
recipe.method: Fit visibilities of NOEMA and ALMA 3 mm and 2 mm observations, then convert Rayleigh-Jeans dust continuum at rest-frame 850 µm (Hughes et al. 2017 prescription) and CO(3-2)/CO(4-3) line emission to molecular gas masses
assumptions: CO-SLED of star-forming galaxies at z = 2.0 - 2.7 from ASPECS (Boogaard et al. 2020)
α_CO derived using mass-SFR-metallicity relation from Genzel et al. (2015) and metallicity dependence of α_CO from Tacconi et al. (2018)

recipe.goal: Analyze cluster-wide and galaxy-level star formation and gas scaling relations
recipe.method: Evaluate ΣSFR/M_halo evolution, scale member SFRs to z = 2.5 to compare with the SFMS, examine radial distribution of stellar mass and starburstiness, and normalize µ_gas and τ_gas to A3COSMOS field relations
key_parameters: z = 2.5 reference redshift for SFMS scaling
assumptions: SFMS normalization and redshift evolution from Schreiber et al. (2015)
Field galaxy scaling relations µ_gas(z, M_*, R_SB) and τ_gas(z, M_*, R_SB) from Liu et al. (2019)
